claim: SofT-GFP shows oscillatory recruitment to single hyphal tips of Arthrobotrys flagrans with a mean period of 137±17 (SD) seconds (n=164 in 18 hyphae) without other hyphae in their vicinity.
source: We monitored SofT-GFP in A. flagrans growing on low-nutrient agar (LNA) and observed oscillatory recruitment of SofT to single hyphal tips with a mean period of 137±17 (SD) seconds (n=164 in 18 hyphae) without other hyphae in their vicinity (Figure 1a, d, and e, Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of SofT-GFP oscillation periods in single hyphae, with specific quantitative data (mean, standard deviation, sample size).

claim: 85 ± 4% (mean ± SD) of hyphal tips showed SofT-GFP fluorescence without a fusion partner (n=50).
source: We measured SofT-GFP signals at hyphal tips and found that 85 ± 4% (mean ± SD) showed fluorescence without a fusion partner (n=50) hyphal tips, experiment repeated three times, (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of SofT-GFP fluorescence at hyphal tips, with quantitative data from repeated experiments.

claim: Hyphae without SofT-GFP recruitment at their tips were unable to fuse.
source: Hyphae without SofT-GFP recruitment at their tips were unable to fuse, suggesting that they could not recognize each other (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b, Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data showing that hyphae lacking SofT-GFP recruitment do not undergo fusion.

claim: Hyphae without SofT-GFP recruitment at their tips could not recognize each other.
source: Hyphae without SofT-GFP recruitment at their tips were unable to fuse, suggesting that they could not recognize each other (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b, Video 2).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that hyphae without SofT-GFP recruitment cannot fuse.

claim: Hyphae without SofT-GFP recruitment were still able to undergo cell fusion if other hyphae induced hyphal fusion.
source: However, these cells were still able to undergo cell fusion if other hyphae induced hyphal fusion (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data showing that hyphae without SofT-GFP can fuse when induced by other hyphae.

claim: Recruitment of SofT-GFP to the hyphal tip and cell fusion were observed on potato dextrose agar (PDA).
source: Recruitment of SofT-GFP to the hyphal tip and cell fusion were also observed on potato dextrose agar (PDA), suggesting that nutrient availability would not be the sole cause of inducing the observed dynamics (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data showing SofT-GFP recruitment and cell fusion on PDA medium.

claim: Nutrient availability is not the sole cause of inducing the observed SofT-GFP dynamics.
source: Recruitment of SofT-GFP to the hyphal tip and cell fusion were also observed on potato dextrose agar (PDA), suggesting that nutrient availability would not be the sole cause of inducing the observed dynamics (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that SofT-GFP dynamics occur on both low-nutrient and high-nutrient media.

claim: The mCherry-tagged orthologue of A. nidulans chitin synthase B (DFL_009443) oscillated at growing hyphal tips with a mean period of 125±37 (SD) seconds (n=50 in 7 hyphae).
source: The fluorescent fusion protein oscillated at growing hyphal tips with a mean period of 125±37 (SD) seconds (n=50 in 7 hyphae) (Figure 1b, d, and e, Video 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of mCherry-ChsB oscillation periods at hyphal tips.

claim: SofT-GFP localized at the same time at growing tips as mCherry-ChsB.
source: To compare the oscillations of SofT and ChsB, we created a strain with both proteins labeled. SofT-GFP localized at the same time at growing tips as mCherry-ChsB (Figure 1e, Video 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data from co-localization experiments with dual-labeled strains.

claim: mCherry-ChsB showed a wider frequency distribution and shorter periods than SofT-GFP.
source: However, mCherry-ChsB showed a wider frequency distribution and shorter periods.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis of oscillation frequency distributions between the two proteins.

claim: The localization of mCherry-ChsB appears to be independent of SofT.
source: Thus, the localization of mCherry-ChsB appears to be independent of SofT (Figure 1f).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that ChsB shows different oscillation patterns than SofT.

claim: Localization and oscillation of mCherry-ChsB at the tip were not affected by deletion of sofT.
source: Indeed, localization and oscillation of mCherry-ChsB at the tip were not affected by deletion of sofT (Figure 1f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from a sofT deletion mutant showing normal ChsB localization and oscillation.

claim: Deletion of chsB in A. nidulans is detrimental for hyphal growth.
source: Deletion of chsB in A. nidulans is detrimental for hyphal growth and was therefore not analyzed in A. flagrans (Borgia et al., 1996; Fukuda et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies on A. nidulans.

claim: SofT consists of 1213 amino acids with a predicted N-terminal disordered region (AA1–540), a WW domain (AA505–533), and a putative C-terminal phosphatase domain (AA676–1213).
source: SofT consists of 1213 amino acids with a predicted N-terminal disordered region (AA1–540), a WW domain (AA505–533), and a putative C-terminal phosphatase domain (AA676–1213) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by protein domain prediction analysis.

claim: A fragment containing the N-terminal region and the WW domain of SofT was sufficient to restore aerial mycelia formation and hyphal fusion in the ∆sofT mutant.
source: A fragment containing the N-terminal region and the WW domain was sufficient to restore aerial mycelia formation and hyphal fusion, while the N-terminal disordered region or the C-terminus was not, emphasizing the significance of SofT-interacting proteins in cell communications (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from complementation experiments with truncated SofT constructs.

claim: The N-terminal disordered region or the C-terminus of SofT alone was not sufficient to restore aerial mycelia formation and hyphal fusion in the ∆sofT mutant.
source: A fragment containing the N-terminal region and the WW domain was sufficient to restore aerial mycelia formation and hyphal fusion, while the N-terminal disordered region or the C-terminus was not, emphasizing the significance of SofT-interacting proteins in cell communications (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from complementation experiments with truncated SofT constructs.

claim: The complementation results emphasize the significance of SofT-interacting proteins in cell communications.
source: A fragment containing the N-terminal region and the WW domain was sufficient to restore aerial mycelia formation and hyphal fusion, while the N-terminal disordered region or the C-terminus was not, emphasizing the significance of SofT-interacting proteins in cell communications (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b, c).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that the WW domain, which mediates protein-protein interactions, is essential for SofT function.

claim: Most A. flagrans hyphae are constantly sending signals in a form of constant 'self-talk', or monologue, possibly to explore the environment for a fusion partner.
source: Our results show that most A. flagrans hyphae are constantly sending signals in a form of constant 'self-talk', or monologue, possibly to explore the environment for a fusion partner.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that single hyphae show oscillatory signaling behavior without fusion partners, combined with speculation about the biological function.

claim: The mathematical model requires that two species in the cell undergo a conversion, with the second species' conversion requiring the first species' transition to have completed to a large extent.
source: This model requires that not one, but two species in the cell undergo a conversion, with the second species' conversion requiring the first species' transition to have completed to a large extent.
evidence: The claim describes a requirement of the mathematical model based on theoretical considerations.

claim: Without sequential conversion, there is no delay between receiving and secreting signal, and the secreting cell would not become non-receptive to its own signal.
source: The reason behind this is that, without this sequential conversion, there is no delay between receiving and secreting signal, and that the secreting cell would not become non-receptive to its own signal (Goryachev et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on theoretical reasoning from a cited model, explaining the necessity of sequential conversion.

claim: Among the abstract model variables, SofT as a signaling component located inside of a hyphal cell connects most closely to variables X1,2 and Y1,2.
source: Among the abstract model variables, SofT as a signaling component located inside of a hyphal cell connects most closely to variables X1,2 and Y1,2 (Figure 2a).
evidence: The claim is based on inference connecting experimental observations of SofT to model variables.

claim: ChsB is located inside the hyphal cells, but localizes differently from SofT and likely does not act as a signaling component.
source: ChsB is also located inside the hyphal cells, but localizes differently from SofT and likely does not act as a signaling component, so that ChsB can be related to the variables A1,2, and I1,2.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from observational data showing different localization patterns between ChsB and SofT.

claim: ChsB can be related to the model variables A1,2, and I1,2.
source: ChsB is also located inside the hyphal cells, but localizes differently from SofT and likely does not act as a signaling component, so that ChsB can be related to the variables A1,2, and I1,2.
evidence: The claim is based on inference connecting experimental observations of ChsB to model variables.

claim: In simulations containing only a single cell, oscillations in different components could be observed, similar to experimental results monitoring components in a single hypha.
source: In simulations containing only a single cell, similar to the experimental results monitoring the components in a single hypha, oscillations in these different components could be observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by mathematical modeling results that reproduce experimental observations.

claim: When placing two cells in the simulation at different distances, oscillations of these two cells appear uncoordinated at long distances (monologue), and anti-phasic at short distances (dialogue).
source: When placing two cells in the simulation at different distances (d) from each other, oscillations of these two cells appear uncoordinated at long distances (monologue), and anti-phasic at short distances (dialogue) (Figure 2b–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by mathematical modeling results showing distance-dependent coordination of oscillations.

claim: High extracellular concentrations of the signaling component (Z1 and Z2) are attained only briefly, when one cell has secreted the component, and the other cell has not yet taken it up again.
source: The role of the signaling component in the dialogue at a short distance can be seen in our simulations: high extracellular concentrations (Z1 and Z2) are attained only briefly, when one cell has secreted the component, and the other cell has not yet taken it up again (Figure 2c).
evidence: The claim is supported by mathematical modeling results showing temporal dynamics of extracellular signaling components.

claim: The back-and-forth exchange of signaling component via secretion into and uptake from the extracellular space represents a physically credible mechanism to establish the cell-to-cell dialogue at a short distance.
source: This back-and-forth exchange of signaling component via secretion into and uptake from the extracellular space represents a physically credible mechanism to establish the cell-to-cell dialogue at a short distance.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from mathematical modeling results about the mechanism of cell-to-cell communication.

claim: When implementing a simulation that mimics the growth of two hyphae toward each other, a transitory phase where the uncoordinated oscillations (two monologues) become mutually entrained into anti-phasic oscillations (dialogue) can be seen.
source: When we implement a simulation that mimics the growth of two hyphae toward each other in the form of a distance that decreases over time, a transitory phase where the uncoordinated oscillations (two monologues) become mutually entrained into anti-phasic oscillations (dialogue) can be seen (Figure 2e).
evidence: The claim is supported by mathematical modeling results showing the transition from monologue to dialogue.

claim: The same regulatory mechanism, based on a signaling component that is exchanged via the extracellular space, can explain the transition from single-cell oscillatory growth to anti-phasic synchronization between two approaching cells.
source: As seen in these simulation results, the same regulatory mechanism, based on a signaling component that is exchanged via the extracellular space, can explain the transition from single-cell oscillatory growth to anti-phasic synchronization between two approaching cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from mathematical modeling results about the underlying mechanism.

claim: The simulations imply a transitory phase during which both cells' dynamics slow down, just before entering into the dialogue and speeding up again.
source: Crucially, these simulations also imply a transitory phase, during which both cells' dynamics slow down, just before entering into the dialogue and speeding up again (Figure 2e).
evidence: The claim is supported by mathematical modeling results showing critical slowing down during the transition phase.

claim: The 'critical slowing down' is typical in phases where a system transitions from one type of dynamic behavior to another type of dynamic behavior, due to being 'caught in between' two types of behavior during the transition.
source: This 'critical slowing down' is typical in phases where a system transitions from one type of dynamic behavior to another type of dynamic behavior, due to being 'caught in between' two types of behavior during the transition (Damineli et al., 2022; Quail et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from cited literature about critical slowing down in dynamical systems.

claim: Initially, the oscillations in two approaching hyphae appeared uncoordinated (orientation phase) but then transitioned to anti-phasic oscillations characteristic of the cell-to-cell dialogue.
source: To experimentally assess the transition from two 'monologues' to a coordinated 'dialogue', we monitored SofT in two approaching hyphae. Initially, the oscillations in the two hyphae appeared uncoordinated (orientation phase) but then transitioned to anti-phasic oscillations characteristic of the cell-to-cell dialogue (Figure 3a and b, Video 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of SofT dynamics in approaching hyphae.

claim: The frequency of SofT oscillations during the cell-to-cell dialogue had a mean period of 104±28 [SD] seconds (n=173 in 18 hyphae).
source: The frequency of SofT oscillations during the cell-to-cell dialogue (mean period of 104±28 [SD] seconds, n=173 in 18 hyphae) was comparable to the frequency in single hyphae and was not influenced by the presence of nematodes (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of SofT oscillation periods during cell-to-cell dialogue.

claim: The frequency of SofT oscillations during the cell-to-cell dialogue was comparable to the frequency in single hyphae.
source: The frequency of SofT oscillations during the cell-to-cell dialogue (mean period of 104±28 [SD] seconds, n=173 in 18 hyphae) was comparable to the frequency in single hyphae and was not influenced by the presence of nematodes (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis of oscillation frequencies between single hyphae and interacting hyphae.

claim: The frequency of SofT oscillations during the cell-to-cell dialogue was not influenced by the presence of nematodes.
source: The frequency of SofT oscillations during the cell-to-cell dialogue (mean period of 104±28 [SD] seconds, n=173 in 18 hyphae) was comparable to the frequency in single hyphae and was not influenced by the presence of nematodes (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing oscillation frequencies in the presence and absence of nematodes.

claim: Oscillations in both hyphae slowed down during the transitory phase that precedes the coordinated cell-to-cell dialogue, as expected from simulations.
source: As expected from our simulations of a dynamic transition into coordinated oscillations, oscillations in both hyphae slowed down during the transitory phase that precedes the coordinated cell-to-cell dialogue (Figure 3b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations that match predictions from mathematical modeling.

claim: MakB-mCherry showed oscillatory recruitment to the nuclei of hyphae with a mean period of 130±33 (n=45 in 8 hyphae) in the absence of neighboring hyphae.
source: We monitored the localization of MakB tagged with mCherry and observed oscillatory recruitment of MakB to the nuclei of hyphae with a mean period of 130±33 (n=45 in 8 hyphae) in the absence of neighboring hyphae and a mean period of 117±19 (n=57 in 8 hyphae) during the cell-to-cell dialogue (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Video 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of MakB-mCherry oscillation periods in single hyphae.

claim: MakB-mCherry showed oscillatory recruitment to the nuclei of hyphae with a mean period of 117±19 (n=57 in 8 hyphae) during the cell-to-cell dialogue.
source: We monitored the localization of MakB tagged with mCherry and observed oscillatory recruitment of MakB to the nuclei of hyphae with a mean period of 130±33 (n=45 in 8 hyphae) in the absence of neighboring hyphae and a mean period of 117±19 (n=57 in 8 hyphae) during the cell-to-cell dialogue (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Video 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of MakB-mCherry oscillation periods during cell-to-cell dialogue.

claim: SofT-GFP and MakB-mCherry were oscillating in the same phase without other hyphae in their vicinity.
source: Interestingly, co-localization of SofT-GFP and MakB-mCherry in the same hyphae revealed that both proteins were oscillating in the same phase without other hyphae in their vicinity (Figure 3d and e, Video 7), which is opposite to the so far observed anti-phasic oscillations observed during the cell dialogue (Fleissner et al., 2009; Haj Hammadeh et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations from co-localization experiments.

claim: In-phase oscillation of SofT-GFP and MakB-mCherry in single hyphae is opposite to the anti-phasic oscillations observed during the cell dialogue.
source: Interestingly, co-localization of SofT-GFP and MakB-mCherry in the same hyphae revealed that both proteins were oscillating in the same phase without other hyphae in their vicinity (Figure 3d and e, Video 7), which is opposite to the so far observed anti-phasic oscillations observed during the cell dialogue (Fleissner et al., 2009; Haj Hammadeh et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of current experimental data with previously published observations.

claim: Decoupling of SofT-GFP and MakB-mCherry oscillations into the anti-phasic cell dialogue occurred during the transitory phase where the growth slowed down.
source: Additionally, we observed that decoupling of SofT-GFP and MakB-mCherry oscillations into the anti-phasic cell dialogue occurred during the transitory phase where the growth slowed down (Figure 3f, Video 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of the transition from in-phase to anti-phasic oscillations.

claim: The transition from a 'monologue' to a 'dialogue' includes the decoupling of SofT and MakB oscillations.
source: These results indicate that the transition from a 'monologue' to a 'dialogue' include the decoupling of SofT and MakB oscillations.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations of oscillation dynamics during the transition.

claim: ChsB showed oscillating recruitment to the tips of interacting cells with mean periods of 103±26 (SD) seconds (n=105 in 11 hyphae).
source: The underlying hypothesis that the same oscillation mechanism acts during the monologue- and dialogue-type dynamics is further substantiated by the observation that, similar to single hyphal growth, not only SofT and MakB but also ChsB and actin filaments visualized by Lifeact-GFP showed oscillating recruitment to the tips of interacting cells with mean periods of 103±26 (SD) seconds (n=105 in 11 hyphae) and 103±27 (n=106 in 10 hyphae), respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a, b, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of ChsB oscillation periods during cell-to-cell dialogue.

claim: Actin filaments visualized by Lifeact-GFP showed oscillating recruitment to the tips of interacting cells with mean periods of 103±27 seconds (n=106 in 10 hyphae).
source: The underlying hypothesis that the same oscillation mechanism acts during the monologue- and dialogue-type dynamics is further substantiated by the observation that, similar to single hyphal growth, not only SofT and MakB but also ChsB and actin filaments visualized by Lifeact-GFP showed oscillating recruitment to the tips of interacting cells with mean periods of 103±26 (SD) seconds (n=105 in 11 hyphae) and 103±27 (n=106 in 10 hyphae), respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a, b, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of Lifeact-GFP oscillation periods during cell-to-cell dialogue.

claim: The observation that ChsB and actin filaments show oscillating recruitment to the tips of interacting cells substantiates the hypothesis that the same oscillation mechanism acts during the monologue- and dialogue-type dynamics.
source: The underlying hypothesis that the same oscillation mechanism acts during the monologue- and dialogue-type dynamics is further substantiated by the observation that, similar to single hyphal growth, not only SofT and MakB but also ChsB and actin filaments visualized by Lifeact-GFP showed oscillating recruitment to the tips of interacting cells with mean periods of 103±26 (SD) seconds (n=105 in 11 hyphae) and 103±27 (n=106 in 10 hyphae), respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a, b, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that multiple proteins show similar oscillation patterns in both monologue and dialogue states.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ concentrations showed robust oscillations that were coordinated between two approaching hyphae.
source: A central assumption underlying the cell-to-cell dialogue in our model is that hyphae communicate by passing back and forth a shared signaling component, Z. Considering the central role of Ca2+ in many types of cellular excitatory dynamics, and previous results that suggest that Ca2+ is involved in the cell-to-cell dialogue (Palma-Guerrero et al., 2013; Simonin et al., 2010; Fu et al., 2011; Fu et al., 2014), we monitored intracellular Ca2+ concentrations using the genetically encoded fluorescent reporter R-GECO. The fluorescent signals showed robust oscillations that were coordinated between two approaching hyphae (Figure 4a and b, Video 10; Zhao et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations using the R-GECO Ca2+ reporter.

claim: The mean oscillation period of R-GECO was 104±33 (SD) seconds (n=160 in 24 hyphae), comparable to the other markers during the cell-to-cell dialogue.
source: The mean oscillation period of 104±33 (SD) seconds (n=160 in 24 hyphae) was comparable to the other markers during the cell-to-cell dialogue (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of R-GECO oscillation periods and comparison with other markers.

claim: Simultaneous visualization of R-GECO and GFP-ChsB showed synchronized oscillation with similar periods, indicating the anti-phasic oscillations of growth during the chemotropic interaction of the two hyphae.
source: Indeed, simultaneous visualization of R-GECO and GFP-ChsB showed synchronized oscillation with similar periods, indicating the anti-phasic oscillations of growth during the chemotropic interaction of the two hyphae (Figure 4d and e, Video 11).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations from dual-labeling experiments.

claim: The anti-phasic oscillations of growth during the chemotropic interaction were coordinated in anti-phase in interacting hyphae.
source: This phenomenon was coordinated in anti-phase in interacting hyphae.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of coordinated oscillations between interacting hyphae.

claim: Signaling and growth during the cell-to-cell dialogue are highly synchronized and possibly mediated by the uptake of Ca2+.
source: These results indicate that signaling and growth during the cell-to-cell dialogue are highly synchronized and possibly mediated by the uptake of Ca2+.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental observations of synchronized Ca2+ and growth oscillations, combined with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: At an EGTA concentration of 5 mM, cell-fusion events were never observed after incubation for 16 up to 72 hr.
source: To further test the role of Ca2+, we depleted Ca2+ from the media by adding the Ca2+ chelating agent EGTA to LNA containing 1 µM CaCl2. At an EGTA concentration of 5 mM, cell-fusion events were never observed after incubation for 16 up to 72 hr (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of cell fusion in Ca2+-depleted conditions.

claim: Hyphal growth of A. flagrans was reduced in Ca2+-depleted conditions, but germination of spores was unaffected.
source: In addition, hyphal growth of A. flagrans was reduced, but germination of spores was unaffected.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of growth and germination in Ca2+-depleted conditions.

claim: Fluorescence of R-GECO was not detectable in Ca2+-depleted conditions.
source: Fluorescence of R-GECO was not detectable in these Ca2+-depleted conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of R-GECO fluorescence in Ca2+-depleted conditions.

claim: mCherry-ChsB still localized at hyphal tips in Ca2+-depleted conditions, however, no obvious oscillating dynamic recruitment was observed.
source: mCherry-ChsB still localized at hyphal tips, however, no obvious oscillating dynamic recruitment was observed (Figure 4f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of ChsB localization in Ca2+-depleted conditions.

claim: mCherry-ChsB localized directly to the plasma membrane at the tip in Ca2+-depleted conditions, without prior accumulation at the Spitzenkörper, confirming the importance of Ca2+ for well-regulated pulsatile secretion.
source: mCherry-ChsB localized directly to the plasma membrane at the tip, without prior accumulation at the Spitzenkörper, confirming with previous reports the importance of Ca2+ for well-regulated pulsatile secretion (Kurian et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and comparison with previous reports.

claim: The localization of GFP-SofT to hyphal tips was abolished after the addition of 5 mM EGTA, indicating Ca2+-dependent recruitment to the plasma membrane.
source: The localization of GFP-SofT to hyphal tips was abolished after the addition of 5 mM EGTA, indicating Ca2+-dependent recruitment to the plasma membrane (Figure 4g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of SofT localization in Ca2+-depleted conditions, with inference about Ca2+-dependence.

claim: Reducing the external media concentration of signaling components in simulations abolished oscillations.
source: In line with these experimental results, reducing the external media concentration of signaling components in our simulations also abolished oscillations (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by mathematical modeling results that match experimental observations.

claim: External Ca2+ concentrations of up to 100 mM did not influence hyphal fusion.
source: On the other hand, external Ca2+ concentrations of up to 100 mM did not influence hyphal fusion.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of hyphal fusion at high Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: Extracellular Ca2+ is important in the signaling mechanism that underlies the monologue implicated in pulsatile cell extension as well as the synchronization of oscillations into a cell-to-cell dialogue.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that extracellular Ca2+ is important in the signaling mechanism that underlies the monologue implicated in pulsatile cell extension as well as the synchronization of oscillations into a cell-to-cell dialogue (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations showing the effects of Ca2+ depletion.

claim: Particles of diameter of approximately 3 nm or less can traverse the distance at which two hyphae synchronize at a sufficiently short time to support synchronization.
source: An estimate calculation indicates that particles of diameter of approximately 3 nm or less can traverse the distance at which two hyphae synchronize at a sufficiently short time to support synchronization (for details, see Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by theoretical calculations based on diffusion physics.

claim: The 3 nm diameter limit would include Ca2+ ions as well as Ca2+-binding proteins, but not secretory vesicles as the component that is exchanged between the hyphae.
source: This diameter would include Ca2+ ions as well as Ca2+-binding proteins, but not secretory vesicles as the component that is exchanged between the hyphae.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the calculated size limit and knowledge of typical sizes of biological molecules.

claim: Punctate localization of SofT orthologue was observed throughout the hyphae in A. nidulans, resembling that seen in A. flagrans.
source: During our study we identified and localized the SofT orthologue in A. nidulans. While we observed punctate localization throughout the hyphae resembling that seen in A. flagrans, we did not observe any tip oscillations in A. nidulans during various cultivation conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of SofT localization in A. nidulans.

claim: No tip oscillations of SofT were observed in A. nidulans during various cultivation conditions.
source: During our study we identified and localized the SofT orthologue in A. nidulans. While we observed punctate localization throughout the hyphae resembling that seen in A. flagrans, we did not observe any tip oscillations in A. nidulans during various cultivation conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of SofT dynamics in A. nidulans.

claim: No hyphal fusion events were observed in A. nidulans.
source: Furthermore, we did not observe any hyphal fusion events.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of A. nidulans hyphal behavior.

claim: Aspergillus species are known to rarely undergo vegetative cell fusion under laboratory conditions, compared to other fungi.
source: It is worth noting that Aspergillus species are known to rarely undergo vegetative cell fusion under laboratory conditions, compared to other fungi (Macdonald et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from cited literature.

claim: figA single gene deletion resulted in a colony phenotype.
source: figA single gene deletion resulted in a colony phenotype, however, both gene deletion mutants still performed cell fusions and trapped nematodes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of the figA deletion mutant.

claim: Both figA and figB gene deletion mutants still performed cell fusions and trapped nematodes.
source: figA single gene deletion resulted in a colony phenotype, however, both gene deletion mutants still performed cell fusions and trapped nematodes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of the figA and figB deletion mutants.

claim: A double-deletion strain of figA and figB could not be generated, suggesting at least one protein to be essential for growth.
source: We were unable to generate a double-deletion strain, suggesting at least one protein to be essential for growth.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the inability to generate a double-deletion mutant.

claim: Fungal hyphae communicate with each other before they fuse and alternate between signal sender and signal perceiver functions.
source: Fungal hyphae communicate with each other before they fuse and alternate between signal sender and signal perceiver functions, or between talking and listening if compared to people.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from previous studies on fungal cell-to-cell communication.

claim: The same signal oscillations occur in hyphae without any other hyphae in the vicinity.
source: Interestingly, the same signal oscillations occur in hyphae without any other hyphae in the vicinity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of signal oscillations in single hyphae.

claim: Upon appearance of a fusion partner, the monologue transits into a dialogue.
source: We named this phenomenon 'monologue' and show that - upon appearance of a fusion partner - the monologue transits into a dialogue.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations of the transition from monologue to dialogue.

claim: At the molecular level the phenomenon may be explained by an interference of the signaling molecules of two approaching hyphae.
source: At the molecular level the phenomenon may be explained by an interference of the signaling molecules of two approaching hyphae.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a molecular mechanism based on inference from observations.

claim: The threshold concentrations for the switch between sending and receiving could be reached too early to be processed by the downstream components and hence the machinery would be disturbed until both hyphae respond to the common signal concentrations between the hyphal tips.
source: The threshold concentrations for the switch between sending and receiving could be reached too early to be processed by the downstream components and hence the machinery would be disturbed until both hyphae respond to the common signal concentrations between the hyphal tips.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a mechanism for the transitory phase based on inference.
